title: Recovery Readiness Auditor
problem: A configured backup schedule does not establish a usable recovery.
implementation: The source project audits recovery-readiness evidence. The new recovery notebook separately checks fictional RTO, RPO and application-validation results.
evidence: Source-linked project plus executed educational fixture; no restore of a production workload was performed.
next: Retain a dated restoration log, data-integrity check and business acceptance record for an actual recovery test.

title: Infrastructure Dependency Analyzer
problem: A change can affect services through dependencies that a flat server list hides.
implementation: Model resources and directed dependency edges, then inspect the assumptions behind an impact path before using it in a change review.
evidence: The linked project source is the implementation record. A dependency path is a hypothesis about impact until checked against the real environment.
next: Compare a known service dependency with observed configuration and record stale, missing and directional edges.

title: Employee Lifecycle Toolkit
problem: Joiner, mover and leaver changes cross identity, access and ownership boundaries.
implementation: Keep requested changes, approval, actual effects and rollback evidence as separate records; idempotency matters when a workflow resumes.
evidence: Source-linked automation project. This content release did not execute identity changes or validate a customer environment.
next: Use a sandbox account and a bounded access matrix to test creation, modification, denial and cleanup before operational use.

title: Asset Inventory Reconciler
problem: Repeated or malformed inventory input can duplicate records or conceal inconsistencies.
implementation: The foundation companion demonstrates schema rejection, atomic SQLite insertion, injected rollback and matching-payload retries.
evidence: The new companion is executed locally; it does not establish that the separately linked project was deployed or that inventory data are accurate.
next: Define matching keys and conflict ownership, then test duplicate, missing and contradictory source records.

title: Kubernetes Operations Lab
problem: A running pod can still be unable to serve traffic.
implementation: Separate startup, readiness, liveness, endpoint membership and service response when investigating a failure.
evidence: Source/manifest evidence and an executed probe-decision fixture; no live cluster rollout was performed in this release.
next: Run a controlled dependency outage in a disposable cluster and preserve pod events, endpoints, restarts and application responses.

title: Advanced Computing Learning Library
problem: An attractive simulation needs assumptions and reproducible numerical checks.
implementation: The authored sequence connects linear algebra, AI mechanisms, quantum state calculations and performance bounds.
evidence: Executed CPU teaching companions with exact or analytic references. They do not establish hardware advantage or graduate-level certification.
next: Choose one calculation, reproduce it independently and identify the experiment needed to extend its scope.

title: Cloud & Systems Knowledge Library
problem: Catalog size can be confused with individually authored depth.
implementation: Eight existing lessons now have scoped reviews, 40 explained questions and runnable foundation notebooks. Forty-one linked study companions add bounded extensions.
evidence: 8,000 legacy record IDs and 300 legacy path IDs remain stable; the new sequence does not reclassify every generated practice entry as reviewed.
next: Retain predictions, failed cases, source locators and integration artifacts while using self-reported progress.

title: Project MIND Agent Workbench
problem: Evidence-looking words cannot independently verify a claimed outcome.
implementation: The existing workflow preview organizes a dry-run plan; the new companion compares actual typed artifacts with explicit acceptance criteria and tests replay.
evidence: Deterministic local workflow and executed in-memory coordination fixtures; no live LLM agents, external tools or distributed consensus run.
next: Add persisted attempts, artifact schema versions and stale-result rejection before connecting a new external execution boundary.

title: Engineering Portfolio
problem: Content changes must preserve the approved experience and remain reviewable.
implementation: The upgrade uses scoped lesson overrides and appended study sections while preserving the baseline corpus, shared ambience and protected engines.
evidence: Review-branch implementation and local checks. A branch or runtime package is not evidence of OSU deployment.
next: Review the exact commit, package hashes, browser evidence and outstanding acceptance gates before a separately approved deployment.

title: Quantum Phase Estimation
problem: Linear phase error can be misleading near the zero/one boundary.
implementation: The existing probability model now reports circular sample RMSE alongside its retained linear statistic; a notebook independently computes ideal probabilities by inverse DFT.
evidence: Classical ideal-state simulation and toy uniform-mixture model; no controlled hardware unitary or calibrated device noise.
next: Compare exact-grid, off-grid and wrap-boundary phases, then distinguish exact distributions from finite-shot samples.

title: One Qubit, Two Outcomes
problem: Computational-basis probabilities alone hide relative phase.
implementation: The existing general pure-state lab varies both θ and φ and measures X, Y and Z. New companions check probabilities and amplitude-damping density operators.
evidence: Executed ideal-state calculations and classical browser simulation; not a quantum device or a two-qubit hardware experiment.
next: Use θ=90°, φ=90° to distinguish Y certainty from Z randomness, then compare a pure state with a mixed state.

title: Emergent Systems Explorer
problem: A coherent-looking animation can conceal time-step or seed effects.
implementation: The existing seeded oscillator model is paired with a separate fixed-fixture Euler refinement comparison and an ensemble extension task.
evidence: Deterministic browser simulation plus executed CPU convergence fixture. No claim that the model reproduces fundamental physics or a physical universe.
next: Hold initial conditions fixed for time-step checks, then compare multiple seeds at each coupling strength.

title: Geometry & Physics Lab
problem: Saved predictions, live calculations and research extensions need distinct evidence.
implementation: The protected lab retains its calculation modules and six recorded GNP cases. New notebooks recompute metrics and check the restricted diffusion/inverse models.
evidence: Historical GNP inference plus new metric auditing. The optional pinned-upstream adapter is separate from the checked CPU notebooks.
next: Run an equal-information normal-estimation comparison before making a broad model superiority claim.

title: Providing Energy from Fusion
problem: A technical presentation explains a topic but is not an experimental energy demonstration.
implementation: The existing presentation and media remain available as authored communication artifacts.
evidence: Presentation/media evidence; this upgrade did not reproduce a fusion experiment or alter the protected video.
next: Use claim-specific references and distinguish plasma physics, engineering gain and whole-system economics when extending the presentation.

title: Crown & Ash
problem: A launcher, source implementation and a playable engine are different acceptance surfaces.
implementation: The existing chess launcher and protected engine files remain separate from the learning companions.
evidence: Engine bytes preserved in this content release. New learning-model checks do not imply a new full-game acceptance run.
next: Use the established chess browser gate for launch, interaction, restart and return before deployment.

title: Evil Wizard
problem: A production-only game export must remain a complete versioned unit.
implementation: The existing launcher retains the protected host export boundary; content work does not replace its runtime, PCK or WASM assets.
evidence: Production export preservation remains a separate gate. No claim that notebook tests validate the hosted game.
next: Run the established hosted-export launch and relaunch checks in the target environment.
